newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened weaker in quiet trade on Wednesday, largely disregarding recent economic reports, with dealers focused instead on taking profits on recent gains, analysts said.

"If you look at some of the Canadian numbers that were just out they are pretty healthy numbers. Certainly that's a factor. But I think that the market just has had a good run and they (traders) are looking more to take some profits than anything else," said one T-bill dealer with a Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 2.86 percent from 2.84 percent at Tuesday's close.
The dealer said there was little account activity in the market and prices were being largely set by traders and dealers taking profits.

Analysts said the money market is now looking ahead to a speech and press conference by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen in Quebec City. Thiessen begins speaking at 1215 EDT/1615 GMT and is expected to hold his press conference at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.21 percent from 3.20 percent. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 3.66 percent from 3.61 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
